about: What a finding's citations are resolved against, as DATA. A `cites-resolve` check names one resolver here; the resolver's `kind` is one of three ways of looking something up (file-line, commit, row), its `pattern` finds the citations in a text, and `roots` names the repositories by the name a citation starts with. Adding a repository or a row pattern is adding a row here, with no code edit. A root whose folder is not on the computer running the check makes the check unevaluated, never passed.

resolvers.meaning: <root>/<path>:<line>; the line of the file at the root's ref must hold the quoted text when the check names a quote field.
A commit hash; it must exist in one of the roots and be dated after the date the check's `after` field holds.
A row id in the person's own records; the row must exist.
